dial.summary: Macro remains broadly constructive with 5/8 indicators supportive — real yields ticked down to 2.60% (DFII10 Nov 5), DXY holds at 102.33 (Friday close) as the lone headwind, ISM Manufacturing holds at 55.5 for October; BTC perpetual funding normalized to 0.0087% on November 8 as markets absorbed the October 30 crash, BTC.D holds at ~59.3% with TOTAL at ~$2.60T, and no alt-rotation catalyst is in view — classic accumulation setup ahead of the November 10 CPI release.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro G4 aggregate (US/Euro Zone/China/Japan) holds at ~$104.3T as of September 2026 (104,317B); October G4 data not yet published — MacroMicro typically updates mid-month following the reference month, so October G4 update expected mid-November 2026; US M2 at $23.41T in Sep 2026 (+5.7% YoY, next US M2 release November 24) confirms no YoY contraction; 4-week Aug→Sep change +$0.64T (+0.6%) exceeds flat threshold — trend UP; Bitrue broader global estimate ~$103.66T; status supportive (4-week trend up); held unchanged from Nov 7 run — October G4 data publication pending mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: October 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.5% (released November 2, 2026), beating consensus 54.6%, up 1.0pp from September's 54.5%; 10th consecutive expansion month; Production sub-index 59.0 (highest since Nov 2021), New Orders 55.5, Prices 75.2 (9th consecutive above 70); 4-week trend UP (Sep 54.5 → Oct 55.5, +1.0pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising); next ISM Manufacturing release December 1, 2026 (November data); value unchanged — monthly series, October reading is current.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot 102.33 as of Friday November 6, 2026 close (Trading Economics confirms ~102.30, Dealplexus ~101.59 intraday); no weekend market data available — November 8 is Sunday; rallied +0.77% on Nov 6 after October NFP beat (+165K vs ~65K consensus); 4-week trend UP — from ~101.5–101.8 range (Oct 5–7) to 102.33 (Nov 6), net change approximately +0.68% exceeds the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind (DXY above 100 — must fall below 97.5 for supportive); prior 52-week high 102.95 (Oct 14, 2026).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) at 2.60% on November 5, 2026 (FRED H.15, latest available; Nov 4 was 2.64%, Nov 3 was 2.65%, Nov 2 was 2.62%); updated from 2.63% (Nov 6 estimate) to 2.60% based on FRED data; 4-week trend DOWN — from ~2.93% on September 29 to ~2.60% on November 5, approximately -33bps; real yields have declined as nominal 10Y fell on Democrat midterm fiscal restraint expectations and then partially retraced post-NFP; status supportive (falling trend — the headwind rule requires rising AND above 2% simultaneously, only one condition met with current declining trend).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: 2s10s spread at +35bps as of November 6, 2026 close (down 3bps on the day from +38bps on Nov 5 as NFP bear-flattened the front end); corrected from previous +0.30% estimate to +0.35% based on search data showing Nov 5 at +38bps and Nov 6 at +35bps; curve recovering from September low of ~+25bps; 4-week trend FLAT — from approximately +30–32bps around October 7 (recovering off Sep lows) to +35bps on November 6, approximately +5bps at the boundary of the flat threshold; 52-week range 20–74bps; status neutral (positive but not sustainably steepening on a 4-week basis).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,748,145M ($6.748T) for week ended November 4, 2026 (FRED updated November 5; next H.4.1 release November 12); prior readings: Oct 28 $6,745,635M, Oct 21 $6,753,604M, Oct 14 $6,755,639M; 4-week change Oct 7 → Nov 4: balance sheet oscillating in a narrow ~$10B band, essentially flat; balance sheet stabilized post-QT-pause (QT ended December 2025); YoY +2.4% from ~$6.59T (Macrotrends); status supportive (flat, no aggressive QT, overnight rates stable); held unchanged — next WALCL update November 12.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass BTC perpetual funding rate (position-weighted) at 0.0087% per 8h as of November 8, 2026 (volume-weighted 0.0081%); normalized from the near-zero 0.0019% reading on November 7 as market digested the October 30 crash deleveraging; 30-day perspective: OKX Aug 5 – Nov 2 average was 0.0056% per settlement, Oct 20 snapshot was 0.01% (convextrade), current 0.0087% — trend FLAT (oscillating between 0.005–0.01% range, no clear directional drift over 4 weeks); CoinGlass benchmark: >0.01% bullish, <0.005% bearish — sitting just below the benchmark; status supportive (well below 0.04% headwind threshold).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: DefiLlama total stablecoin market cap ~$290.1B as of November 8, 2026 (USDT ~61% dominance); total crypto market cap ~$2.60T (BTC dominance ~59.3%); implied stablecoin dominance $290.1B/$2.60T ≈ 11.2% (down from 11.4% Nov 7 as TOTAL recovered slightly to $2.60T from $2.57T); 30-day trend UP — October 1 dominance was ~10.2% ($291B/$2.86T), now 11.2% as TOTAL fell while stablecoins held; status neutral — headwind requires rising dominance AND rising TOTAL simultaneously; TOTAL is still well below Oct 1 level ($2.60T vs $2.86T) so headwind condition not met, but dominance is not falling so supportive condition not met either.

upcoming.title: CPI (October 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS releases October 2026 Consumer Price Index at 8:30 AM ET — the last inflation report the Fed receives before the December 9 FOMC vote (November CPI publishes Dec 10, the day after the decision); consensus: +0.3% MoM headline, 3.7% YoY, core +0.2% MoM / 2.6% YoY; October NFP beat (+165K, unemployment 4.1%) and elevated ISM Prices (75.2) raised the bar for a soft print; a hot print above 3.7% would seal a December hike, while a print near 3.0% could keep December in play as a pause.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended November 8, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims released Wednesday November 12 (shifted one day earlier from normal Thursday due to Veterans Day federal holiday November 11); first labor pulse following the strong October NFP (+165K, unemployment 4.1%); a print below 215K would reinforce December hike odds; a spike above 230K would re-open debate about labor-market cooling ahead of the FOMC blackout period (November 28).

upcoming.title: PPI (October 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS releases October 2026 Producer Price Index at 8:30 AM ET — consensus: +0.3% MoM headline and core; September PPI was 6.3% YoY and ISM Manufacturing Prices remains at 75.2 (9th consecutive above 70), signaling persistent upstream cost pressure; completes the November inflation picture alongside CPI (Nov 10) and provides the final inflation input set for the December FOMC dot plot revision.
